facts.text: The mermaid hook's `input` handler ignores bare `continue`/`go on`/`keep going`; any other interactive or rpc prompt sets `eligible` via `wantsMermaidExplanation` and resets `requested`. `session_start` and `session_switch` clear both flags.

In `extensions/mermaid-response/extension.ts`, `message_end` runs `repairMermaidResponse` on final assistant text parts. `turn_end` sends `mermaidFollowup` with `triggerTurn` only when eligible, not already requested, not aborted, no pending messages, text is at least 80 characters, and no complete mermaid fence exists. `requested` is set before dispatch.

`repairMermaidResponse` in `.pi/lib/context/mermaid-response.ts` changes only single-token flowchart/graph `--  >` or sequenceDiagram missing-colon lines, and only when `validateMermaid` confirms the fix. It skips lines containing quotes, brackets, braces, or pipes. An unavailable parser is treated as valid.

`.pi/lib/tern/run.ts` binds no extension UI context, and the repo has no `setUIContext` call. Its no-op UI denies `confirm` and returns no selection or input. `.pi/lib/tern/bridge.ts` says extension prompts are answered by native Tern dialogs in `ext-ui.ts`.
evidence: docs/reference/pi-tern-extension-default-blocker.md#Why a Pi extension alone cannot select TSP at startup

facts.text: The docs state that a Pi extension cannot make bare `pi` start the Tern/TSP frontend, because Pi starts its TUI before extension binding. They record the user's constraint as extension-only, so the opt-in runner `.pi/lib/tern/run.ts` is not the default.
evidence: docs/reference/pi-tern-extension-default-blocker.md#Why a Pi extension alone cannot select TSP at startup

facts.text: `docs/reference/tern-pi-shell-dispatch.md` describes a guarded `pi()` shell function that sends bare interactive `pi` in Tern panes to `.pi/lib/tern/run.ts`. Argument-bearing, noninteractive, and non-Tern uses keep native `pi`. This is configuration, not an extension.
evidence: docs/reference/tern-pi-shell-dispatch.md#Bare `pi` in Tern: local shell dispatch for dogfooding

facts.text: `docs/reference/tern-integration-status.md` records the Pi (trebol) Tern frontend as not OMP 1:1. It lists extension UI dialogs/approval overlays, live cancellation, and resume as unverified, and advises against using it as the default for authorization-sensitive work.
`docs/reference/tern-integration-status.md` contains the `## Pi (trebol)` and `## Code Puppy` sections that record Tern integration evidence for each lane.
`extensions/trebol-toggle/index.ts` registers `ctrl+n` as the Trebol toggle shortcut, wrapped by `installTrebolShortcut` in `.pi/lib/runtime/trebol-shortcut.ts`.
